summary: Static preflight only. Existing epoch guards suppress a late probe's UI result and notification starts, but do not establish cancellation, drained persistence, or terminal callback fencing.

findings.claim: shutdown clears the interrupted-sample marker immediately while probe.sample can still be awaited. resume also acknowledges that same marker even when the previous live sample has not finished. A quit during either interval can therefore appear clean despite unfinished work.
findings.recommendation: With the existing gated probe, stop before releasing completion and assert the marker remains owned by the active sample; repeat pause/resume before release. Clear only on confirmed completion/drain, or retain an interruption marker if termination cannot wait. Distinguish acknowledging a previous-launch interruption from an active sample.

findings.claim: Cancelling loopTask/eventSampleTask does not cancel every sampleNow caller, and PersistentMonitoringProbe has no cancellation checks before native scanning, recordScanSlice, or later retention. Its store operations can continue after a stop; the controller's epoch check runs only after persistence returns.
findings.recommendation: Define a cancel-before-publication versus drain-in-flight contract and own the active sample independently of its caller. Add deterministic gates before work/publication and injected volume/scan sources for the concrete probe; cancel at each gate and assert the allowed writes and drain completion. Do not claim rollback of an already committed transaction.

findings.claim: shutdown is terminal for canSample, but not for lifecycle transitions: resume and resumeAfterSystemWake can still publish active status afterward; prepareForSystemSleep can also change status. Removing workspace observers does not retract Tasks already queued by their callbacks.
findings.recommendation: Guard terminal state before lifecycle/settings/marker mutations. Directly call shutdown followed by wake, resume and sleep; assert unchanged status/history/settings and zero additional probe calls. Replay a queued power callback through a small injected dispatcher, without invoking NSWorkspace.

findings.claim: Notification delivery is fenced only before its await. An already-started delivery has no controller-owned cancellation or validity token, so a delivery suspended before its external send may finish after pause/sleep/quit. The existing late-probe test covers delivery not starting, not delivery already in progress.
findings.recommendation: Inject a delivery fake that gates immediately before recording a send. Start an alerting sample, await that gate, stop, then release it. Require no new send after stop through a delivery-side cancellation/epoch check at the send boundary; distinguish this from a notification already handed to the OS.

findings.claim: Collector callbacks capture no epoch and only check canSample before awaiting noteEventGap. A callback from the previous lifecycle may run after resume, or resume its await after a new callback, then cancel/replace the newer eventSampleTask. This is a lifecycle integration condition, separate from hint receipt semantics.
findings.recommendation: Fence callback entry and post-await continuation by collector/lifecycle generation. Replace the concrete collector dependency with a narrow restart/stop protocol; retain fake callbacks and gate noteEventGap to replay old/new ordering. Inject a controllable sleeper for debounce/loop tests; also cover a busy follow-up queued across pause/resume without wall-clock sleeps.
